summary: Arjun took an order for 5 cartons Maggi, 2 cartons Parle-G and 1 peti Tata Tea. Sharma ji will pay by UPI on Friday, with delivery and the bill due the same day. Britannia is offering 15-day credit and has already sold Good Day and Marie into the outlet. Sharma ji asked for credit, and Arjun gave no real answer.
score_reason: Arjun took an order and fixed a payment date, but he did not explain any scheme, did not check visibility, and left a direct credit demand tied to a Britannia threat unaddressed.

coaching.tip: You opened with a stock check on Maggi, which led straight into a 5-carton order. You also closed by fixing a clear payment date (Friday UPI) and tying it to delivery. Keep that discipline.

When Sharma ji asked for credit to match Britannia, 'dekhte hain' left the threat open. Next time, acknowledge it, explain the current scheme on Parle-G, and promise a specific answer after checking with your manager.
Sharma ji mentioned Good Day and Marie from Britannia. Use that moment to pitch Sunfeast or Mom's Magic as an alternative. Also check his biscuit shelf share before leaving.

debrief: Arjun, Sharma General Store ka visit theek raha. Paanch carton Maggi, do carton Parle-G aur ek peti Tata Tea ka order mila, aur Friday ka UPI payment bhi pakka karwaya, bahut badhiya. Ek cheez try karo: jab Sharma ji ne Britannia ke pandrah din ke credit ki baat ki, 'dekhte hain' se aage jaao, current scheme samjhao aur manager se baat karke clear jawab do. Agla step: Friday ko delivery bill ke saath, aur credit par update.
